newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea SEC finds insider trading in Korea KDK.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea SEC finds insider trading in Korea KDK.

text.p: South Korea's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said on Wednesday it had found insider trading involving Korea KDK Co shares.

The SEC has asked state prosecutors to investigate the chief executive of brokerage firm Korea M&A Co on suspicion of having utilised unannounced information on the transfer of management rights within Korea KDK Co, an SEC statement said.
Korea M&A could not be immediately reached for comment.
Separately, the SEC said it had found the head of Korea KDK Co in violation of share ownership regulations.
The chief executive of Korea KDK, an electronics firm, had not reported his ownership of more than five percent in Korea KDK's share capital to market authorities, the statement said.
Ownership of over five percent in a company and any ownership change thereafter must be reported to the securities authorities under current regulations, it said.
Officials at Korea KDK could not be immediately reached to comment on the SEC statement.
